data.title: Thailand SEC proposes 5 million Baht daily cap on stablecoin transfers — Why?
data.description:
Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has proposed a set of new rules to regulate stablecoin transactions conducted through licensed digital asset operators.

Announced on 12th November, the draft notification aims to prevent cryptocurrencies and stablecoins from being used for money laundering, cybercrime, and bypassing regulations governing international money transfers.

Here, it’s worth noting that this update came soon after September’s public consultation. During the same, the regulator collected feedback from industry participants.

What is the purpose behind the 5 million Thai baht limitations?

As it stands, the SEC has incorporated those changes into the latest draft. It is now seeking further public comments until 26th November.

In this, one of the key proposals is to introduce a daily transfer limit of 5 million Thai baht per customer at each regulated digital asset operator. That said, the limit would apply separately to incoming and outgoing stablecoin transfers. However, the value of these transactions must also be consistent with the customer’s declared income and financial position.

However, it’s important to note that transfers between a customer’s own accounts at two SEC-supervised operators would be exempt from the limit, provided both operators follow the Travel Rule.

SEC’s game plan for stablecoin regulations

Simultaneously, the SEC also wants to strengthen wallet ownership verification. In this, the SEC has enabled customers to deposit stablecoins from their own verified wallets and withdraw them to wallets registered in their names.

Additionally, operators would also need to follow the Travel Rule, analyze customers, identify suspicious accounts, and track transactions connected to high-risk wallets.

These requirements would be done in order to make it harder for criminals to move illicit funds through regulated platforms.

Other limitations that are a must

Finally, the proposal also introduces stricter responsibilities for exchanges and brokers. Exchanges would have to publicly disclose their market makers and the digital assets for which they provide liquidity. Meanwhile, brokers would be prohibited from using liquidity providers for stablecoin-to-Thai baht trading pairs.

Besides that, brokers and dealers offering off-platform transactions would face a minimum transaction threshold of 3 million baht and would have to publish trading prices for transparency. Brokers would no longer be allowed to arrange off-platform trades directly between customers.

Taken together, these steps would help the SEC combat crimes that are concerning the stablecoin ecosystem in Thailand.

Final Summary

  • The proposal has introduced a daily transfer limit of 5 million Thai baht per customer at each regulated digital asset operator.
  • Brokers and dealers offering off-platform transactions will face a minimum transaction limit of 3 million baht.

data.title: TRON, Tether and Chainalysis launch task force as crypto hacks hit $8.78B
data.description:
On the 12th of November, TRON, Tether, and blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis jointly launched the Digital Crime Task Force (DCTF), an initiative aimed at identifying and disrupting illicit financial activities involving Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the TRON blockchain.

In this plan, TRON will contribute its blockchain network expertise, and Tether will provide support as the issuer of USDT. Meanwhile, Chainalysis will bring its blockchain intelligence, investigative expertise, and AI-powered monitoring tools.

The scam epidemic spreads like wildfire

One of the major reasons behind the initiative is the growing sophistication of crypto-related financial crime. According to Chainalysis, AI-enabled scam operations were 4.5x more profitable than traditional scams in 2025. Meanwhile, impersonation scams increased by more than 1,400% year over year.

DefiLlama further reported that the crypto industry recorded $8.78 billion across 328 hacks in 2026 so far. This is the highest annual loss recorded in its database. In fact, the five biggest hacks together contributed more than 85% of the overall losses.

Interestingly, the number of attacks increased around 2.7 times compared to 2025, while the median loss declined from $1.07 million to $510,000. This suggests that hackers are carrying out more frequent attacks, although most incidents involve relatively smaller amounts.

Criminal sophistication takes center stage

Seeing this rise, the organizations believe that traditional approaches, which often depend on victims reporting crimes or investigators identifying suspicious funds, are no longer sufficient. Instead, they want to identify potential threats before criminals can move their funds.

Remarking on the same, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said,

Criminals are using AI to move faster than ever, and waiting for a victim to report a crime is no longer good enough

This remark comes as Tether has already frozen more than $7 billion linked to illicit activities while working with over 360 law enforcement agencies across 73 countries.

That said, the new task force will therefore be built on these efforts by focusing on proactive investigations and faster coordination. It will also accept tips and asset-freezing requests directly from law enforcement agencies.

What’s more?

Needless to say, the DCTF will investigate several categories of financial crime, including investment and romance scams, stolen funds, cryptocurrency hacks, terrorist financing, North Korean cyber operations, and much more.

This coincided with the FBI recently launching ‘Operation Blackout,’ a coordinated international crackdown targeting scam compounds across Southeast Asia, Africa, and the Middle East that defraud American citizens through fake investment platforms and online impersonation.

Meanwhile, ACAMS has partnered with blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis to strengthen cryptocurrency anti-financial crime training through an updated CCAS certification.

Final Summary

  • The initiative is a joint effort by TRON, Tether, and Chainaysis to combat the growing sophistication of crypto-related financial crime.
  • The crypto industry recorded $8.78 billion across 328 hacks in 2026, marking the highest annual loss recorded in its database.

data.title: Bitcoin dips below $70K – Will $455M in liquidations derail BTC’s price recovery?
data.description:
The crypto markets are bleeding, and so is Bitcoin [BTC], the largest of them all. The total cap of the crypto market is down over 5% in the past 24 hours, as market status turned to extreme fear.

More than $856.01 million in crypto liquidations happened with longs, equating to $771.7 million. Of the total liquidations, Bitcoin accounted for $454.7 million, with longs taking 96%.

As a result, BTC slid below $70,000 and was trading around $68,888, at press time, having lost 6% of its cap. A daily trading volume of $31.90 billion reinforced the sharp decline in price below $70,000.

For Ethereum [ETH], 91% of longs were liquidated from its total of $131.95 million. Other crypto assets saw over $218 million wiped out, with long positions representing 75%.

Can renewed spot demand support recovery?

At the same time, a Bitcoin rebound toward $71,000 was becoming more fragile considering other factors. For instance, the market sentiment from some analysts, like Benjamin Cowen, was shifting.

When replying to his post that bear market makes fools of both bulls and bears, Benjamin Bowen reiterated he thought Q4 could be weak.

This has been the case since the midterm US election results, implying investors were less optimistic as pro-crypto Republicans lost control of the house.

Additionally, monthly spot and futures demand was contracting at an accelerating rate. That of spot was at -280K BTC, while that of perpetual futures was at -82K, a total demand of -362K BTC.

Moreover, Bitcoin ETF outflows reached $300 million on the 11th of November and $48 million the following day. This indicated institutions were consistently withdrawing capital from Bitcoin and the crypto market in general. This adds institutional selling pressure to BTC.

More downside risks emanate from a spike in miner-to-exchange flows this week. The total surged to 2,077 BTC, about 16 times its 30-day average of 127 BTC.

However, it does not confirm selling, as it could mean treasury transfers or management. Though, it could mean miners’ margins are getting squeezed by low prices.

There was more to this nose dive. US demand for BTC was quiet, with the Coinbase Premium Index below -4 from 0.8 in September. This was the deepest average since February, affirming the low demand.

However, there was still a catch. The rallies of 2024 and 2025 all ran with a premium, with several of them starting from such deep discounts.

This could be driven by renewed spot demand as its CVD is closer to neutral, though the improvement did not last there. The Futures taker CVD was dominated by sellers.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin price plunged below $70,000 as liquidations surpassed $455 million, with longs accounting for 96%. 
  • Bitcoin recovery remains fragile amidst weak demand, ETF outflows, and shifting market sentiment.

data.title: Trezor slashes reseller network by 80% following hardware implant discovery – Details
data.description:
Trezor confirmed on the 12th of November that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis contained malicious implants. Fortunately, no customer had reported losing funds.

Still, Trezor urged affected buyers to move their crypto after releasing a firmware fix.

Customers bought those 3 devices between the 20th of August and the 23rd of September through CryptoBilis directly or its Tokopedia and Shopee stores. Trezor examined one device in its lab and identified two more from customer photos.

48 buyers had contacted the company, and at press time, checks were ongoing. Trezor reported that there were no confirmed cases involving other models or resellers.

Why did Trezor urge buyers to move funds?

Apparently, the implants could take recovery phrases and passphrases that appeared on the wallet screen.

On X, a user asked how a software update could stop a physical implant from recording the display. Trezor explained that firmware could “listen to the communication between the MCU and the display,” and the firm has now changed the order of commands needed for the trigger.

Regardless, Trezor still urged buyers to use a fresh recovery phrase because “the update can’t protect a wallet backup that was captured before it.” This advice applied to customers who bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis from March 2026 onward.

The hardware wallet company also urged those using its devices to move funds to a new wallet with a fresh recovery phrase. It told buyers with unused devices to leave them unconfigured. Eligible buyers could contact Trezor Support for a replacement or a refund where shipping limited their options.

How did the Ledger case shape Trezor’s response?

Trezor dropped CryptoBilis on the 9th of October after reports of tampered Ledger devices sold through them. A customer also flagged a suspected Safe 5 implant on the 28th of October.

Trezor issued a warning two days later, saying that it cut its reseller network by about 80% and tightened rules on sourcing, storage, and access.

This brought the debate back to what self-custody protects, and as Ledger CEO Pascal Gauthier said,

Everybody will be hacked at some point. Perfect security doesn’t exist.

 

Final Summary

  • Trezor confirmed that there were three tampered Safe 5 wallets sold through CryptoBilism, but no one had experienced losses yet.
  • However, affected buyers still need a wallet with a fresh recovery phrase.

data.title: Bitcoin dominance hits 61%, but THIS will decide when is altcoin season!
data.description:
Altcoins have been waiting for their moment all year. Bitcoin [BTC] keeps taking it from them. However, it would seem now that the latter’s market share could decide who wins the next few weeks.

The ‘undeafeated’ Bitcoin

Coinglass’s Altcoin Season Index had a reading of 42 at press time.

Anything above 75 ordinarily counts as altcoin season. This means that the press time reading still leaned towards Bitcoin.

There’s numbers to back this up too. According to CryptoRank, for instance, Bitcoin was up 16.6% over the last 90 days.

Only 31 coins on its list did better!

Bitway [BTW] has risen by about 220%, Quant [QNT] went up 184%, Midnight Network [NIGHT] by 172% and Raydium [RAY] by 152%. Stacks and NEAR also doubled on the price charts.

That’s where the excitement ends though.

A lot of the big names didn’t even keep up with BTC. Solana [SOL], for instance, went up a measly 10% over the same stretch. Binance Coin [BNB] also rose by 10.6%, and Chainlink [LINK] outdid them… with 12%.

So yes, a few altcoins are having a great run. Most of the rest are just watching Bitcoin ride off into the sunset.

Who’s the winner?

At the time of writing, BTC.D was at 60.9%.

On the weekly chart, that’s a range that’s been narrowing for more than a year. The top of that has been sliding since late 2025. The bottom has been going up from around 57%.

Right now, it’s pushing right against the top.

If dominance breaks above 61.5%, Bitcoin will maintain its lead and altcoins will stay stuck in the mud. If it diverges near 61%, that would mean that the latter group will get a little breathing room.

A drop below 58% is where things could really swing towards Ethereum [ETH] and the rest of the market though.

For context, its dominance peaked at about 66% back in mid-2025. We are nowhere near that yet.

Until then, the market should lie in wait. Altcoin holders will really want that rejection at the 61%-level though.

Final Summary

  • Only 31 altcoins surpassed Bitcoin’s 16.6% gains over the last 90 days.

  • BTC.D at 61% will decide whether altcoins can recover.

data.title: How TSMC’s employee data leak raises questions over cloud security
data.description:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) confirmed on the 12th of November that some current and former employees’ personal information had appeared online without authorization.

As per reports, the hacker has asked for 3 BTC, which is worth about $220K, for a database they claimed held 46,000 employee records. The hackers claimed to have 6.9 GB of data and threatened to publish it within a week without a buyer. However, no payment has been publicly verified, as of press time.

What data did the TSMC leak expose?

For the unaware, TSMC makes chips for other companies. They said that the leaked records matched data held by a cloud provider. Notably, these records included names, national ID numbers, and banking details, according to Taiwan News.

The company’s own review found no evidence of a break in its systems. As of the latest update from the company, they were notifying affected staff and working with the cloud provider and investigators.

Looking at the impact this news had, TSMC’s U.S. listed shares opened 4.53% lower at $394.62 on the 12th of November. They recovered some ground to close at $405.49, down 1.90% on the day. By the way, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) followed a similar path, opening 4.33% lower and ending the session down 1.03%.

With chip stocks also under pressure, it was difficult to tell how much of TSMC’s drop was due to the leak.

Needless to say, this leak surfaced before a volatile session for chipmakers and AI cloud providers. The semiconductor ETF recovered much of its early loss, even though the individual chip stocks went in different directions.

Notably, Nvidia fell 4.34% after announcing CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation. On the other hand, AMD and Broadcom both gained, rising 5.86% and 5.54%, respectively.

Furthermore, the Kobeissi Letter identified intraday losses in Nebius, CoreWeave, and IREN.

Who was responsible for protecting the records?

TSMC’s annual filing says it sets security or confidentiality requirements for outside providers. Going back to 2023, it cut off data exchange with supplier Kinmax after a breach exposed server setup information.

On X, a user wrote,

That vendor connection actually raises liability questions that don’t get enough attention in breach discussions

Another user shared a different perspective,

Your employer picked the vendor. you just get the breach notice

The type of employee data matters for a different reason. Binance said its October theft followed a campaign that targeted engineers before reaching its wallet signing service.

Furthermore, the ransom of 3 Bitcoin [BTC] puts the listing in the context of a wider trade in stolen data. Moreover, Chainalysis tracked $87.5 million in on-chain volume at fraud shops in 2025.

Final Summary

  • TSMC has confirmed an employee data leak involving records that matched data held by a cloud provider.
  • The hacker asked for 3 BTC. The claim of 46,000 records remains unverified by TSMC.

data.title: SUI crypto’s 26% drop sparks bottom calls – Is a ‘short‑term bounce’ next?
data.description:
Sui [SUI] crypto token was trading at $0.7799 as of writing, after a drop of 4.6% in the past 24 hours. In fact, in just one month the altcoin has fallen by over 26%, which has raised eyebrows across the community.

However, the SUI Community has taken this drop from an optimistic lens and suggested that SUI’s price may be nearing its bottom. They argue that sell-side liquidity, such as stop-loss orders, is piling up just below the low range.

Their theory, based on Wyckoff-style analysis, is that price may briefly dip below the range to trigger those orders, then reverse sharply upward and break out.

Hence, they added,

If the candles break lower, we could see a short‑term bounce back soon.

For context, this analysis was done when SUI was trading around $0.81, and since then the altcoin has fallen even further.

Crypto community on SUI

Echoing similar sentiments, another X account added,

However, not everyone shared the same sentiment, as another analyst shared his opinion and said,

So, if looked at carefully, SUI has already experienced its major price decline and is now in a consolidation phase. During this period, impatient investors may sell their holdings out of frustration, while patient investors continue accumulating.

Many believe that this phase could eventually lead to an expansion phase, potentially triggering another upward price move.

What triggered Sui’s price fall?

This comes as Suiet, a self-custodial wallet for the Sui blockchain, has announced plans to shut down development and maintenance, with its API services ending on the 14th of November.

All of this also resulted in Sui’s total value locked (TVL) falling more than 23% in a month, from $510.9 million to $394.27 million, raising more questions.

However, with more than $100 million worth of stablecoins entering the Sui ecosystem in less than a month, hope remains.

What’s next for SUI?

Meanwhile, the 24-hour liquidation heatmap for SUI/USDT on Binance from CoinGlass shows that the brightest clusters sit above the current price near $0.81, $0.82, and $0.83. So, if the price pushes up, it could trigger a wave of short liquidations that adds fuel to the rally.

However, there is also a cluster near $0.775 to $0.78 and another around $0.76, which is where the recent dip already swept through, so those long positions have largely been flushed. This somewhat fits the Sui Community’s “shake-out” idea, since the dip below the range likely cleared out leveraged longs before the bounce.

Remarking on the same, known crypto analyst, Ted Pillows added,

Late longs have been wiped out, and now shorts are getting aggressive. Only a matter of time before these shorts will get liquidated.

Final Summary

  • SUI experienced its major price decline and is now in a consolidation phase.
  • Sui’s TVL fell more than 23% in a month, from $510.9 million to $394.27.

data.title: How Ethereum staking hit a record 36.3% despite ETH’s price drop
data.description:
Ethereum’s [ETH] staking ratio has reportedly reached an all-time high (ATH)  of 36.3%, accounting for more than one-third of ETH’s total circulating supply. Well, the rising staking ratio suggests that an increasing number of ETH holders are choosing to lock up their tokens rather than sell or actively trade them.

This comes as Ethereum’s validator queues show that at press time, 911,938 ETH was waiting to be staked with a 16-day, 7-hour wait. Meanwhile, 264,211 ETH was queued to exit with a 5-day, 16-hour wait, plus a 7-day sweep delay.

Both queues are limited by the same churn rate of 256 per epoch, meaning only a fixed amount of ETH can join or leave each epoch, which is why a big backlog translates into longer waits.

In other words, more people want to stake than unstake right now, but the entry line is slowly shrinking, and exiting takes roughly 12-13 days in total once the sweep delay is included.

Total staked ETH so far

This comes as the total ETH staked rose from about 42.1 million ETH (roughly 34.5% of supply) in mid-August to about 44.5 million ETH (around 36.5%) at press time. Since late October the climb has resumed steadily.

Of this, BitMine earned $121.4 million from staking and validation activities, accounting for approximately 97% of its total revenue. By the 8th of November, the largest Ethereum DAT held 6.07 million ETH, of which 5.22 million ETH was staked.

That said, the company also estimates that these holdings could generate around $309 million in annual staking rewards, based on an estimated 2.65% yield and an ETH price of $2,234.

On the other hand, SharpLink has accumulated 31,363 ETH in staking rewards as of 9th November. Its strategy also includes liquid staking through Lido, allowing it to receive wstETH in return for its deposited ETH.

Active validators tell a different story

All of this happened while the active validators moved in the opposite direction. As per charts, they held near 900K through mid-September, peaking around 912K. But again, they dropped sharply from mid-September to mid-October, falling to about 815K, and have since drifted down to roughly 807K, with a small additional drop on the last day or two.

However, the price action of ETH trading at $2,042.94 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours but a 15.5% drop in the past week sparks concern. This comes as Ethereum faces renewed selling pressure after losing its $2,250 support level. However, Vitalik Buterin’s recent push to position ETH as a store of value suggests hope.

Final Summary

  • 911,938 ETH was waiting to be staked while 264,211 ETH was queued to exit.
  • Total ETH staked rose from about 42.1 million ETH in mid-August to about 44.5 million ETH.

data.title: Everyone’s selling XRP right now, but why?
data.description:
XRP [XRP] has been sliding on the charts for weeks, and it looks like everyone’s selling their stash right now.

Whales have been steady though. They’ve been trading big, but we don’t quite know whose side they’re on.

XRP Futures and Spot traders join hands… to sell

Cryptoquant’s Futures Taker CVD has been sell-dominant since late August. That hasn’t changed yet so, two and a half months straight.

The only time this year Futures traders leaned buy-heavy was in the beginning of 2026. In that time, XRP has gone from $1.55 in late September to $1.05 now.

Spot traders used to turn a blind eye, but not anymore. For the most part, their CVD was neutral this year. There were some buy-heavy stretches in January, February and May.

That changed in October. Now, the Spot Take CVD is also sell-dominant. This is the first time that’s happened all year!

That matters more than you think. Futures selling might just be traders betting short. When Spot starts selling too, that would mean that people holding actual XRP may be getting out.

XRP volume is running hot!

Usually, when people trade a coin this much, it’s because the price is rising. With XRP though, that’s not been the case.

Futures volume bubble map went red in late August. Through most of September and early October, it was marked as “overheating.” While that’s slowed down a bit since, it’s still been a fair spike.

Spot followed.

It moved into “heating” in early September, was “overheating” in the middle of the month, and has stayed hot ever since.

Now, put that next to when Spot volume was “cooling” at $1.40.

Both markets are busy right now, but since it’s all during a dip, it may be indicative of selling.

Whales are swinging big, and that could decide what happens next!

Finally, CryptoQuant’s Average Order Size has shown “big whale orders” on Futures and Spot since early October.

That’s happened before as well. Whale-sized orders were all the rage through June, July, and most of August. All this, while XRP went between $1 and $1.25.

Towards the end of August, the price went back to $1.50 on the charts.

As with many others, this metric also only shows how big orders are, and not which way they’re going. Whales could be buying the dip, or walking away.

Either way, they’re the ones moving the most money right now. Whatever they decide at $1 is probably where XRP goes next.

Final Summary

  • XRP Spot traders went sell-dominant for the first time this year!
  • Big whale orders have been active on both markets, despite XRP’s fall towards $1.

data.title: TSMC confirms data breach as hacker demands Bitcoin worth $215K — Details
data.description:
2026 hasn’t been a great year as far as security is concerned. Whether it is Bitget or Binance, every single episode this year has simply highlighted how important it is.

It hasn’t been a great time for chipmakers around the world either. The latest news associated with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company or TSMC is a case in point.

What happened?

TSMC is in the news today after hackers reportedly offered up private information linked to one of the company’s employees on an underground forum. According to the hacker, they have access to over 46,000 records right now. These records will be released publicly if the hackers aren’t paid 3 BTC or $214.7K within one week.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that the hacker in question isn’t exactly holding the information to ransom. At the time of writing, there hadn’t been any demands or efforts to blackmail. Instead, the hacker is looking for a buyer, any buyer, for the information in question.

For its part, TSMC acknowledged that “data of some current and former employees was disclosed without authorization.” However, the company was also quick to stress that there is no real evidence that any of its security systems were compromised. Its preliminary investigative report suggested that,

… this data matches the data in the system service of a certain cloud service provider.

TSMC also clarified that the data in question wasn’t associated or linked with any clients or production.

Right now, the popular chipmaker is working with cloud service providers and cybersecurity agencies to better understand what happened. It is also taking measures to make sure this doesn’t happen again.

Here, it is worth clarifying that the present case isn’t exactly a traditional ransomware attack. Instead, it’s a simple case of data breach since no malware was used and TSMC hasn’t been locked out of its system.

Another year, more ransomware attacks

Still, this is an industry that isn’t exactly new to ransomware episodes. Back in 2023, for example, TSMC was targeted by the LockBit group who demanded $70M.

According to Black Kite’s ransomware report, for instance, there has been a 24% YoY increase in ransomware disclosures compared to the previous disclosure period. It also found,

The threat actor ecosystem grew right alongside the victim count, reaching 127 active groups by the close of the period and 146 by June 2026.

Finally, the report in question also revealed that the manufacturing sector accounted for around 22% of all ransomware attacks. Professional, scientific, and medical services accounted for another 18% of the total share. The ransomware breach that targeted DaVita Inc. back in 2025 and affected over 2.7M patients is perhaps the most famous example of the same.

Is Nvidia off the hook now?

The timing is interesting. Especially since news of this incident coincided with Nvidia hogging the headlines after CEO Jensen Huang resigned following an extramarital scandal. In fact, one can argue that the news has taken the spotlight off TSMC for now.

As expected, this has had a corresponding effect on the sector, related industries, and their performances. For instance, the likes of IREN, Core Scientific, and TeraWulf all fell on the charts in the hours following the aforementioned resignation.

Final Summary

  • TSMC’s data is reportedly being held to ransom for 3 BTC.
  • TSMC was quick to acknowledge that none of its systems were compromised.
